To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We propose a novel security notion for searchable encryption, called multi-user security, which captures the security requirements of a multi-user searchable encryption scheme.

(i) the existing single user searchable encryption schemes are not secure in a multi-user setting; (ii) the security notions for single-user searchable encryption do not capture the security requirements for multi-user searchable encryptions; and (iii) we propose a set of security definitions for multi-user searchable cryptography, and provide a construction which is proven secure in the standard model under standard assumptions.
we introduce a novel notion of security for multi-user searchable encryptions and present a construction that achieves this notion of security in the standard model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
three major questions: (1) What are the security notions for multiuser searchable encryption? (2) How can the security notions be achieved?

the following two questions: (i) what are the security requirements of searchable encryption in the multi-user setting?; and (ii) how can we construct a searchable encryption scheme satisfying these requirements?
the design, analysis, and implementation of searchable encryption in the multi-user setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the security notion for the multi-user scenario we propose is the strongest notion for multi-user searchable symmetric encryption.
our construction is secure under the strongest security notions that we can define.
the construction is secure under our security notions and the security notions capture the security properties of searchable encryption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose the first practical multi-user searchable encryption scheme with provable security.
we provide the first construction of a searchable encryption scheme which is secure in a multi-user setting.
we propose and realize the first searchable encryption scheme that allows multiple data owners and multiple queriers to jointly use the same database.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the multi-user setting, the data owner should encrypt the database in a different way from the way that a single user encrypts the database.
, in a multi-user setting, the security of a searchable encryption scheme should be defined with respect to the entire system, and should not be limited to only a single user.
the multi-user scenario is significantly more challenging than the single-user scenario.
